summary.name: Warp Factories
summary.one_liner: Warp Factories is a platform for defining autonomous software-development "factories" as code, where fleets of coding agents handle work from issue or chat triggers through to mergeable pull requests.
use_cases: Automating dependency bumps and flaky test triage
Routing issues from Slack or Linear to AI agents that open PRs
Benchmarking models on your own engineering tasks to cut cost per PR
Running coding agents with shared repos, secrets and MCP tools
Self-hosting AI coding agents inside your own VPC
Verifying agent-made UI changes with screenshots or video
summary.what_it_does: The page describes Warp Factories, where a factory is defined in a YAML file (factory.yaml) that connects repositories, secrets, MCP servers, cloud providers, and work sources like Slack, Linear, or Jira. Agents inherit model, runner, and environment defaults from the definition, and specialized agents can override them. Factories can be triggered by an issue, a Slack message, or a schedule, and coordinated from triage through review to a PR. The platform says it supports any MCP-capable coding agent and any frontier or open-weight model, chosen per pipeline stage. It also includes evals, model benchmarks, and self-improvement loops, and agents capture screenshots or video to prove their work before a PR ships.
notable: Factories defined as versioned code (factory.yaml) with repos, secrets, MCP servers and cloud roles
Works with any MCP-capable agent and any model, including Claude Code and Codex, without requiring the Warp terminal
Runs on Warp's cloud or fully self-hosted in your own VPC
Agents capture screenshots or video to verify their work before opening a PR
caveats: Usage-based pricing priced per agent run; no concrete prices are listed on the page
Page is largely marketing; claims such as cost reductions and PR counts are self-reported by the vendor
